messages:
maria_cs: Escalation: AcmeCorp (tenant acme-42) reports intermittent p99 TTFB spikes on streaming endpoints for ~36h. Non-stream total time looks fine. UI stalls for their users. Ticket #4789

jordan_support: adding kevin_eng + sam_runtime. Trace link + repro attached in ticket: https://tickets.internal/4789/trace/abc123. Customer classifies as high impact.

kevin_eng: Can you paste the exact curl they used and confirm whether this is SSE or h2+trailers? Also which SDK/proxy in front of them?

maria_cs: Repro they gave (minimal):

```
curl -v \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses?model=redwood-large&stream=true" \
  -d '{ "input": "hello" }'
```

Client details from customer: custom multiplexing proxy (internal) using HTTP/2, keepalive=30s, max_chunk_bytes=4096. They see the UI wait for the first chunk a lot.

sam_runtime: Thanks. Quick metrics for tenant acme-42 (last 24h): stream TTFB p50 90ms, p95 360ms, p99 1250ms. Non-stream total p99 ~720ms. So first-chunk/TTFB on streaming is spiking much more.

alyssa_sre: Any edge deploys in the window? Ops-bot shows deploy event: routing-proxy v1.18.3 rolled 24h ago. Also please gather edge-flush logs and proxy frame sizes.

kevin_eng: Hypothesis: small-chunk behavior + http2 flow-control + edge coalescing is causing delayed first-byte flushes for streaming. Quick mitigation we can try: enable a tenant override to force flush chunks at the edge (disable coalescing) so clients see the first chunk immediately. We have a temporary flag: `stream.force_flush`.

maria_cs: Customer is willing to test. Can you give exact steps I can paste?

kevin_eng: Run from console or API. Example API call:

```
curl -X POST "https://console.internal/api/tenants/acme-42/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"stream.force_flush": true, "stream.heartbeat_interval_ms": 250}'
```

That will force smaller chunks to be flushed immediately and add a heartbeat chunk every 250ms as a fallback.

sam_runtime: Good plan. Also consider setting a streaming -> non-stream fallback rule if requests exceed 10s queue/serialize time. We'll canary that for acme-42.

alyssa_sre: For urgent mitigation I'll add a canary routing rule that prefers non-stream responses for this tenant if cumulative wait > 10s. That reduces user-visible stalls while we investigate root cause.

jordan_support: I'll note the proposed mitigations in the ticket and ask them to re-run the same curl (or their app) after we flip the flag. Please ping me when done so I can coordinate verification with the customer.

kevin_eng: Applying tenant override now (ETA ~5m).

ops-bot: feature-flag: stream.force_flush set for tenant acme-42 by kevin_eng @ 3105004550

kevin_eng: Done. Instructed customer to re-run the same command but add header `X-Redwood-Force-Flush: 1` (server will also respect tenant flag if present).

maria_cs: Customer ran test and reports TTFB p99 dropped to ~200ms after change. They still see rare spikes; will keep an eye and share packet captures if it recurs. Marking customer impact reduced for now.

jordan_support: Thanks team — I'll update ticket #4789 with the mitigation steps and monitor. Reopen if they see further regression.
